root_cause.text: The `sps30_i2c_read_meas` function incorrectly calculates the size of the destination buffer `meas` by using `sizeof(num)` (the size of the `size_t` count parameter) instead of `sizeof(*meas)` (the size of the `__be32` buffer element), resulting in an incorrect buffer size being passed to `sps30_i2c_command`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the buffer size argument in `sps30_i2c_command` being corrected from `sizeof(num) * num` to `sizeof(*meas) * num`, and the commit message explains that `sizeof(num)` evaluates to `sizeof(size_t)` (8 bytes on 64-bit) instead of the intended `__be32` element size (4 bytes).

bic_trace_step.reason: In the function `sps30_i2c_read_meas` on line 170, the size of the destination buffer is calculated as `sizeof(num) * num`. Since `num` is of type `size_t`, `sizeof(num)` evaluates to 8 (on 64-bit architectures) or 4 (on 32-bit architectures), whereas the buffer `meas` is of type `__be32 *` (where each element is 4 bytes). This results in an incorrect buffer size being passed to `sps30_i2c_command`.
